method: rules: 3 export+3 import per country from the 633 not drawn on 2026-11-08, then 4 more unstratified from the remaining; clauses: shuffled order of the 116 not drawn on 2026-11-08 (excl. the ALL row), first 2 per country then next 4

rules.rule: Goods, including mail items, worth more than AUD 2,000 or needing an export permit must be entered on an Export Declaration; lower-value goods are exempt. Australia charges no export duty.
rules.statute: Customs Act 1901

rules.rule: Australian native plants and CITES-listed plants need a DCCEEW export permit; live native plants are never exempt.
rules.statute: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999

rules.rule: Australian protected objects, such as significant Aboriginal heritage items, archaeological objects, fossils, meteorites and historical documents, cannot be exported without a permit.
rules.statute: Protection of Movable Cultural Heritage Act 1986
rules.permit: Export permit or certificate under the Act

rules.rule: Counterfeit medical devices cannot be imported under any circumstances.
rules.article: Personal Importation Scheme conditions (TGA; no section cited on page)
rules.statute: Therapeutic Goods Act 1989

rules.rule: Cigarettes, loose and shisha tobacco and heat-not-burn sticks need import permission obtained in advance, and all duty is due at the border; cigars and up to 1.5 kg of oral tobacco are exempt from the permission rule.
rules.statute: Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956

rules.rule: Radio devices sold online, by post or in person must meet ACMA standards; small online sellers face the same rules and penalties as large retailers.
rules.statute: Radiocommunications Act 1992

rules.rule: Mailing plants, seeds, fruit, bark, plant parts and soil is regulated under the Plant Protection Act and CITES; the CFIA permit office handles questions.
rules.statute: Canada Post — Non-mailable matter guide

rules.rule: Goods or technology on the Export Control List, or any goods bound for a country on the Area Control List, need an export permit.
rules.statute: Export and Import Permits Act

rules.rule: Livestock, poultry and animal germplasm may be exported only with proof they meet the importing country's sanitary rules and a CFIA-endorsed export certificate.
rules.statute: Health of Animals Regulations (C.R.C., c. 296)

rules.rule: Animals or plants, or their parts or derivatives, taken or traded in breach of a foreign state's law may not be imported.
rules.statute: Wild Animal and Plant Protection and Regulation of International and Interprovincial Trade Act

rules.rule: Rough diamonds must arrive in a compliant container with a valid, accurate Kimberley Process Certificate from a participant.
rules.statute: Export and Import of Rough Diamonds Act

rules.rule: Imported food must meet Canadian-equivalent safety controls, and the importer must give CFIA import information, including the licence number if licensed.
rules.statute: Safe Food for Canadians Regulations (SOR/2018-108)
rules.permit: SFC import licence for commercial imports

rules.rule: Animals and animal/plant products must be declared for quarantine before export; animals needing isolation are quarantined at designated sites.
rules.statute: 中华人民共和国进出境动植物检疫法

rules.rule: Animal and plant products (e.g. meat products, animal-based pet food) must be declared for export quarantine.
rules.statute: 中华人民共和国进出境动植物检疫法

rules.rule: Each traveller may carry at most RMB 20,000 in or out per trip; no postal-specific cash limit was found.
rules.statute: 中国人民银行公告〔2004〕第18号
rules.quantity_limit: RMB 20,000 per traveller per trip (traveller rule)

rules.rule: All weapons, imitation weapons, ammunition and explosives are banned.
rules.article: 禁止进境物品 第1项
rules.statute: 中华人民共和国禁止进出境物品表 / 中华人民共和国限制进出境物品表（海关总署令第43号）

rules.rule: Unlisted animal/plant products (e.g. tea, dried goods) are quarantined at the international mail exchange and released only if they pass.
rules.statute: 中华人民共和国进出境动植物检疫法

rules.rule: Items on the prohibited carry/post list are returned or destroyed.
rules.statute: 中华人民共和国进出境动植物检疫法

rules.rule: Zoll's list of goods restricted for postal export to non-EU states covers only species protection, dual-use goods, torture goods, rough diamonds, cultural goods and weapons. No national export restriction on e-cigarettes or refill liquids found; destination and carrier rules apply.
rules.statute: Zoll guidance: Einschränkungen (Waren) for postal exports to non-EU states

rules.rule: Dual-use items, including sensitive electronics, telecoms and IT goods and software, may need an export authorisation before shipment outside the EU.
rules.statute: Verordnung (EU) 2021/821 (Dual-Use-Verordnung)

rules.rule: Zoll's list of goods restricted for postal export to non-EU states covers only species protection, dual-use goods, torture goods, rough diamonds, cultural goods and weapons. No national export restriction on tobacco products found; destination and carrier rules apply.
rules.statute: Zoll guidance: Einschränkungen (Waren) for postal exports to non-EU states

rules.rule: If unaccompanied cash of €10,000 or more enters Germany by post or courier, customs may require a disclosure from sender or recipient within 30 days.
rules.statute: Zollverwaltungsgesetz (ZollVG)

rules.rule: Importing signal jammers and laser pointers above one milliwatt is generally prohibited; other electrical and electronic devices must meet EU safety and conformity requirements.
rules.statute: Produktsicherheitsrecht der EU, per Zoll guidance

rules.rule: Sturgeon caviar needs CITES documents when imported by post; unlike travellers, postal imports get no exemption even for small personal quantities.
rules.statute: Artenschutzrecht (CITES), per Zoll guidance

rules.rule: Exporting a controlled drug is prohibited unless an exemption applies or it is done under a Home Office licence and its conditions.
rules.statute: Misuse of Drugs Act 1971
rules.permit: Home Office controlled drug export licence

rules.rule: Exports or re-exports of CITES-listed animals, plants or their parts and products need a CITES permit or certificate issued by APHA.
rules.statute: CITES as applied in GB (Control of Trade in Endangered Species Regulations)

rules.rule: Cash of £10,000 or more carried between Great Britain and a non-UK country must be declared; Border Force may seize any cash suspected of criminal links.
rules.statute: Cash controls (HMRC guidance)

rules.rule: Perfumes with a flashpoint below 60°C are banned from international mail.
rules.statute: Duties and import VAT on gifts (HMRC guidance, international mail)

rules.rule: Importing CITES-listed animals, plants or derivatives needs a CITES permit; posted items need a CN22/CN23 plus the permit, and Border Force may seize items without one.
rules.statute: CITES as applied in GB (Control of Trade in Endangered Species Regulations)

rules.rule: Before placing radio equipment on the GB market, the importer must ensure conformity assessment, required marking and documentation are in place.
rules.statute: Radio Equipment Regulations 2017

rules.rule: Arms include air guns over 2 joules, stun guns, pepper sprays and crossbows over 6 kg; they need Police licences, and Munitions List items need a TID export licence.
rules.statute: Firearms and Ammunition Ordinance (Cap. 238)
rules.permit: Police licence; TID export licence for Munitions List items

rules.rule: Exporters must lodge an export declaration within 14 days; postal packets whose contents are worth under HK$4,000 are exempt from declaration.
rules.statute: Import and Export (Registration) Regulations (Cap. 60E)

rules.rule: Selling, offering for sale, manufacturing, or holding alternative smoking products (e-cigarettes, heated tobacco, herbal cigarettes) for sale is banned, so a Hong Kong seller cannot lawfully sell them abroad.
rules.statute: Smoking (Public Health) Ordinance (Cap. 371)

rules.rule: Importing currency or bearer instruments worth over HK$120,000 as cargo in one batch needs an advance electronic declaration; mail packets are excluded from this cargo rule.
rules.statute: Cross-boundary Movement of Physical Currency and Bearer Negotiable Instruments Ordinance (Cap. 629)

rules.rule: Importing alternative smoking products, including e-cigarettes, heated tobacco, herbal cigarettes and their parts and liquids, is an offence; only transit and air transhipment cargo are exempt.
rules.statute: Import and Export Ordinance (Cap. 60)

rules.rule: Milk and milk drinks, frozen confections and foods with colourings, sweeteners, preservatives or metals face specific import or composition rules.
rules.statute: Public Health and Municipal Services Ordinance (Cap. 132)

rules.rule: Japan does not bar tobacco exports by post, but Japan Post lists tobacco among items most often prohibited by destination countries.
rules.article: あて先の国によって送れないもの
rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）

rules.rule: Items covered by the IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations cannot be sent by international mail by any service or route: fireworks, lighter fuel, gas cylinders, matches, lighters, bleach, pesticides, mercury, wet batteries, dry ice.
rules.statute: 国際郵便として送れないもの（日本郵便：万国郵便条約・航空危険物規則等に基づく禁制品）

rules.rule: The advance report to the Finance Minister for cash or securities above JPY 1 million (or precious metals above the set weight) applies when carried in person; other export modes are exempt under this order.
rules.statute: 外国為替令

rules.rule: Pistols, rifles, machine guns, cannons, their ammunition and pistol parts may not be imported except by persons authorised under other laws.
rules.statute: 関税法

rules.rule: Businesses importing regulated electrical products must notify METI within 30 days of starting and may sell them only with the PSE mark.
rules.statute: 電気用品安全法

rules.rule: Goods infringing patents, utility models, designs, trademarks, copyright, neighbouring rights, circuit layouts or plant breeder rights may not be imported.
rules.statute: 関税法

rules.rule: SingPost will not carry dangerous goods: explosives, compressed gas and aerosols, flammable liquids and solids, oxidisers, toxic substances, radioactive material, corrosives including wet or sealed lead-acid batteries, magnetised items, dry ice.
rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)

rules.rule: Parcel post may leave Singapore without a customs export permit, as may air exports of S$1,000 or less, unless the goods are dutiable or controlled; then a permit is required.
rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995
rules.quantity_limit: Air exports up to S$1,000 permit-free (non-dutiable, non-controlled)

rules.rule: Customs can seize goods about to be exported that are suspected of infringing a registered trade mark, copyright, geographical indication or registered design, on a rights holder's notice or on its own initiative.
rules.statute: Trade Marks Act 1998 / Copyright Act 2021

rules.rule: Tobacco is dutiable at any value. Tobacco arriving by parcel post must follow standardised packaging rules or be returned, and importing for sale needs an HSA tobacco licence.
rules.statute: Tobacco and Vaporisers Control Act

rules.rule: Food imported for sale needs an SFA licence or registration and an import permit for every consignment; receiving and selling food or samples by parcel post still counts as commercial import.
rules.statute: Regulation of Imports and Exports Act 1995

rules.rule: SingPost will not carry dangerous goods into Singapore: explosives, gas and aerosols, flammable liquids and solids, oxidisers, toxic substances, radioactive material, corrosives such as lead-acid batteries, magnetised items, dry ice.
rules.statute: SingPost General Prohibition & Dangerous Goods (carrier rule, IATA DG classes)

rules.rule: Cash, securities, gold and other high-value items above set thresholds must be declared, including when sent by courier or post.
rules.statute: 洗錢防制法

rules.rule: No tobacco export restriction found for parcels.
rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法

rules.rule: Where the importing country requires a phytosanitary certificate, the exporter applies for inspection and a certificate.
rules.statute: 植物防疫檢疫法

rules.rule: Pet food up to 6 kg by post needs no feed-import registration certificate; other import rules (e.g. quarantine) still apply.
rules.statute: 郵包物品進出口通關辦法
rules.permit: Feed import registration above 6 kg; quarantine rules still apply

rules.rule: Sea dangerous-goods channel only: ships carrying dangerous goods need a classification-society carriage document noted on their inspection certificate; the loading rules above are issued under this article.
rules.statute: 船舶法

rules.rule: Personal-use radio terminals (phones, Bluetooth, low-power RF) by post: up to 2 units per shipment with a personal-use undertaking, max 10 per year, adult 18+; 3-10 units need an NCC import approval certificate; no resale.
rules.statute: 電信管制射頻器材製造輸入及申報作業管理辦法
rules.quantity_limit: Post: 2 units/shipment without permit; 10/year per person

rules.rule: Knowingly trafficking in goods bearing counterfeit marks is a federal crime; trafficking expressly includes importing or exporting for commercial gain.
rules.statute: 18 U.S.C. 2320 — Trafficking in counterfeit goods or services

rules.rule: By post, any rough diamond may be mailed out of the United States only if controlled through the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme; otherwise its export by mail is prohibited.
rules.statute: USPS International Mail Manual (IMM)

rules.rule: Lithium batteries may go by international mail only when installed in the device: at most 4 cells or 2 batteries, lithium-ion up to 100 Wh per battery, lithium metal up to 2 g, no lithium marks.
rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail
rules.quantity_limit: Max 4 cells or 2 batteries per mailpiece; 2 mailpieces per consignment

rules.rule: Foreign-made articles, or their containers, must be legibly and permanently marked with the English name of the country of origin unless excepted.
rules.statute: Customs regulations (19 CFR Part 134)

rules.rule: Foreign makers of devices offered for import must register with FDA, list their devices and name a U.S. agent.
rules.statute: Device registration and listing (21 CFR Part 807)
rules.permit: FDA establishment registration and device listing

rules.rule: ENDS devices, parts, accessories and e-liquids are nonmailable, and the PACT Act exceptions do not extend to international mail.
rules.statute: USPS Publication 52 — Hazardous, Restricted, and Perishable Mail

rules.rule: Producers, including distance sellers supplying end users directly, may make batteries, also those inside appliances, available in a Member State only if they or their EPR authorised representative are registered in that Member State's producer register.
rules.statute: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 concerning batteries and waste batteries
rules.permit: Registration in the Member State producer register

rules.rule: Controlled drugs may not be sent by post or express.
rules.statute: 管制藥品管理條例

rules.rule: Exporting regulated mercury-added products is banned, including cosmetics with mercury content above 1 ppm.
rules.statute: Mercury Control Ordinance (Cap. 640)

rules.rule: Chinese national currency is a restricted import.
rules.article: 限制进境物品 第4项
rules.statute: 中华人民共和国禁止进出境物品表 / 中华人民共和国限制进出境物品表（海关总署令第43号）

clauses.text: Not covered: real estate, vehicles (except bikes/hoverboards), businesses, industrial machinery, gift cards and cash equivalents, gold, financial products, NFTs, gambling, donations/crowdfunding, government payments, bill pay, custom-made items for SNAD, collected-in-person items for INR, AUP-prohibited items, Payouts, friends-and-family payments, items for resale.
Withdrawals to an eligible linked bank account by standard transfer or instant payout where available.

The Acceptable Use Policy has no specific entry for live animals, plants or seeds, food, cosmetics, or batteries/hazardous materials. Such goods fall only under the general rule that activity must not violate any law, so legality in the seller and buyer jurisdictions governs.

German Buyer Protection: open a case within 180 days of payment, escalate within 20 days if no agreement. No separate 30-day limit for not-as-described cases appears on the page; changes favouring consumers applied from 15 April 2025.
